newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds plod forward in late trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds plod forward in late trade.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities notched several ticks higher and spreads to Treasuries were unchanged to a fraction wider in late Monday trade, mortgage experts said.
"Its been extremely quiet other than this last little spurt up, which doesn't seem to be on much volume," said one trader at a Midwest firm. "People are just reassessing positions," he said.
Pass-throughs traded 2/32 to 6/32 higher overall, while comparable Treasuries were up 5/32 to 8/32.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0-percent paper was up 3/32 at 100-17/32, yielding 112 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae paper rose 2/32 to 100-17/32, and Freddie Mac issues were up 3/32 at 100-25/32.
Five-year Treasuries were up 5/32 at 6.80 percent, and 10-year notes were up 8/32 at 6.91 percent.
Salomon Brothers reduced its recommended mortgage allocation to a modest underweight, according to Anthony Lembke, co-head of mortgage strategies.
"If you factor in last week's rise in volatility, they look that much more expensive," he said.
Normally, spreads should widen out as volatility increases and narrow as volatility declines, explained Lembke.
But mortgage spreads did not widen last week.
Option-adjusted spreads and mortgage valuations appeared to be at the tight end of their own range, Lembke said.
"We're recommending indexed investors underweight to the aggregate index, and if you're not an indexed investor, it might be time to just sell mortgages and buy Treasuries," he added.
